subsystems.name: Tip array
subsystems.role: provides many atom-manipulating probes that can each pick up and place individual atoms.

subsystems.name: Positioning stage
subsystems.role: moves each tip with sub-atomic precision in three dimensions.

subsystems.name: Control and feedback
subsystems.role: senses when a tip is near an atom and commands precise placement.

subsystems.name: Vacuum and thermal management
subsystems.role: keeps the workspace clean and the atoms still enough to position.

subsystems.name: Feedstock and substrate
subsystems.role: supplies atoms and holds the growing structure in place.

buildSteps.title: Make the tips
buildSteps.detail: Metal wires are etched or electrochemically sharpened to end in a single atom, then arranged as an array on a chip.

buildSteps.title: Integrate actuators
buildSteps.detail: Each tip is bonded to a piezoelectric scanner that can move it in x, y and z with sub-atomic resolution.

buildSteps.title: Build the environment
buildSteps.detail: The array is enclosed in an ultra-high vacuum chamber and cooled to cryogenic temperatures to stop atoms from wandering.

buildSteps.title: Calibrate
buildSteps.detail: Each tip scans a known surface to map its exact position and electrical response.

buildSteps.title: Write control software
buildSteps.detail: Algorithms approach an atom, detect it from the tunneling current, and command the tip to pick it up or drop it.

buildSteps.title: Demonstrate single-atom placement
buildSteps.detail: One tip at a time is used to position individual atoms, a feat already achieved experimentally since 1989.

buildSteps.title: Operate in parallel
buildSteps.detail: All tips in the array are coordinated so they build a structure without colliding or disturbing each other.

buildSteps.title: Assemble a simple object
buildSteps.detail: A few-hundred-atom cluster or quantum dot is built atom by atom to prove the method works.

buildSteps.title: Scale up
buildSteps.detail: More tips, faster actuators and automated error correction are added to build larger flawless crystals.

prerequisites.why: single atoms have been positioned with an STM tip since 1989, proving the basic manipulation principle.
it provides the sub-atomic movements needed to place a tip with atomic precision.
they keep the surface clean and the atoms still enough to be handled.
small arrays of cantilevers exist for probe storage research, but not yet for atom-by-atom assembly.
proposals for building molecules atom by atom exist, but no general working method has been demonstrated.
building a flawless crystal requires detecting and fixing misplaced atoms automatically, which is not yet possible.

pathway.milestone: single-atom manipulation with one STM tip; atomic layer deposition makes uniform films but not positional structures
pathway.unlocks: proof that atoms can be moved deliberately on a surface.

pathway.milestone: small parallel arrays of tips placing atoms in two-dimensional patterns
pathway.unlocks: faster writing and the beginnings of atomically precise surface structures.

pathway.milestone: three-dimensional assembly of simple nanostructures such as quantum dots or tiny perfect crystals
pathway.unlocks: custom materials with electronic or optical properties set atom by atom.

pathway.milestone: atomically precise manufacturing of macroscopic materials with flawless crystal structure
pathway.unlocks: perfect lenses, ultra-strong materials and quantum processors built to atomic specification, if speed and error rates are solved.
